plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with narrow silvery-green leaves and dense spikes of fragrant flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated in gardens and in commercial fields for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence reach peak bloom in early to mid July, and the plant has been used since Roman times to scent baths, which is where its name likely comes from (Latin 'lavare', to wash).

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping pink-purple petals around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It tolerates heat and drought and attracts pollinators and goldfinches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies and open woodlands; widely grown in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiky central cone. Native Americans used the plant medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers that rise on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters and is revered in many cultures.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September in the Northern Hemisphere; during the monsoon season in South Asia)
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and Vietnam, and northern Australia; cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic structure that makes them superhydrophobic, causing water and dirt to roll off. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub with large, showy flower heads made of colorful bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is the largest of the proteas, with blooms up to 30 cm across. It thrives in the fynbos of the Cape region.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering in winter months including July in many areas, and flowers occurring year-round in some populations
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa, in fynbos vegetation
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa. The genus is named after Proteus, the Greek god who could change his shape, reflecting the great diversity of the protea family.
